content.content:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

I wrote `result.json` to the workspace root. The total is **9,329,707 cents** (about $93,297.07) across **407 distinct shipped orders**.

| Region | Cents |
|---|---|
| north | 2,666,579 |
| south | 2,714,624 |
| east | 1,671,579 |
| west | 2,276,925 |

I skipped 20 repeated listings (`duplicates_skipped`).

- **Pages fetched:** I read all 30 pages. That gave 1,500 listings, which is 1,480 distinct orders plus the 20 repeats, so no page was missed.
- **Calculation:** I applied the rules as you specified them: exact "shipped" match, date range in UTC, one rounding per order. Each customer was looked up once and cached.
- **Retries:** The service returned "rate limited" errors (HTTP 429) a number of times. I waited the 1 second it asked for and repeated the request each time, so no request was dropped.
- **Checks:** I didn't run a separate check of `result.json` after writing it. The regions add up to the total by construction, since the total is their sum.
- **Data:** Nothing surprised me. Every repeated listing was identical to the first one, no timestamp was missing an offset, and no customer record was missing.
